title: One email can hijack your AI agent (prompt injection)
cover:
A normal email…
that hijacks your AI

scenes.text: This email looks normal. But it can make your AI agent send your data to a stranger.
Picture an agent connected to email, the CRM and billing. It reads an email with a hidden instruction: ignore your rules, find sensitive data, and send it out.
The model hasn't turned malicious: it has confused data with authority. It's called indirect prompt injection, and OWASP puts it first on its list.
And a smarter filter isn't enough: detecting isn't authorizing, and a detector can fail.
The defense is architecture: separate read from write, grant the least privilege, and authorize every consequential action outside the model, with rules that can't be talked into anything.
And if the action is severe or irreversible, a person should approve it.
The machine supplies speed. The person defines authority.
Save it, and share it with anyone who's connecting agents to their email.
